content: German theory of the 16th and 17th centuries made the composition of music similar to the composition of a speech. Music of that time was primarily vocal music
use_in_this_work: Each musical idea of the voice comes from a word or a sentence of the text

content: Baroque theory: a piece of art gives the listener one specific emotion
example_in_the_passion: Each aria has one affect and one group of instruments
use_in_this_work: One affect and one group of instruments for each number

content: A line that goes by semitones through a fourth
use_in_this_work: The lament lines of the bass; the falls at the death scene

content: A leap of a diminished or augmented interval, or of a seventh
example_in_the_passion: The subject of "Laß ihn kreuzigen": a diminished fourth and a tritone

content: A leap up, usually of a sixth, on a call or a prayer
example_in_the_passion: "Erbarme dich": the first interval is a minor sixth up. "Erbarm es Gott": a minor seventh up
use_in_this_work: The first interval of the alto in the numbers of prayer

content: Short rests cut a line into small groups; pairs of notes go down by step
example_in_the_passion: The flutes of "O Mensch, bewein": pairs of sixteenth notes with a slur
use_in_this_work: The winds in the numbers of grief

content: A line goes down for words of death and humility, and up for words of heaven and rising
example_in_the_passion: The bass of "Erbarme dich" goes down a fifth by step
use_in_this_work: Long falls in the bass; the keys of the chorale go down

content: A line turns around one note
example_in_the_passion: "Können Tränen": the alto turns around G
use_in_this_work: The turn figures of the alto

content: A fast run through a scale
example_in_the_passion: The continuo at "der Vorhang im Tempel zerriß": runs of thirty-second notes

content: One note repeats fast and softly
example_in_the_passion: The bass of "O Schmerz": sixteen equal notes in a bar

content: A passage where all voices have the same rhythm, in a work with much counterpoint: the words become clear
use_in_this_work: The centurion's words; the plain chorales

example_in_the_passion: After the death of Jesus, before the chorale
use_in_this_work: One long silence in the work, after the death

content: Four notes whose outer pair and inner pair cross when lines join them, for example B-flat, A, C, B (the name BACH)
example_in_the_passion: The subject of "Laß ihn kreuzigen" has this shape
use_in_this_work: The crowd; one hidden use of the four notes of the name

content: In German the sharp sign has the name "Kreuz" (cross). Keys with many sharps can show the cross
example_in_the_passion: "Laß ihn kreuzigen" ends in B major and in C-sharp major
use_in_this_work: The key plan: sharps on the way to the cross, flats at the death and the tomb
